title: 1959 AHSME Problem 19
statement: With the use of three different weights, namely, \(1\) lb., \(3\) lb., and \(9\) lb., how many objects of different weights can be weighed, if the objects to be weighed and the given weights may be placed in either pan of the scale?

solutions.text:
Using coefficients \(-1,0,1\) for the weights \(1,3,9,\) balanced ternary represents every integer weight from \(1\) through \[ 1+3+9=13. \] Thus there are \(13\) different positive object weights that can be measured.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Each weight may go with the object, against the object, or remain unused
The weights \(1,3,9\) can represent every integer from \(1\) through their sum
